outcome: maternal complications (preterm labour, anaemia, hypertension, diabetes)
foetal complications (Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR), birth weight discordance, low APGAR score, early neonatal death, foetal malpresentation)
mode of delivery (caesarean section rates and indications)
cohort: 70 mothers with twin pregnancies delivering at JNU Hospital and Medical College, Jaipur between December 2015 and December 2019 were included.
finding: The study found a twin pregnancy incidence rate of 16.5 per 1000 deliveries, with common maternal complications being preterm labour, anaemia, and hypertension, and common foetal complications including IUGR, birth weight discordance, and low APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the main mode of delivery, with foetal malpresentation being the most common indication, and it showed a significant association with hypertension and preterm labour.
followup_time: early neonatal period (up to 7 days post-birth)
birth_weight: Mean weight of first twin was 2.12+/-0.35 kg; mean weight of second twin was 1.97+/-0.30 kg.
